title: The Intern
synopsis: You're seventy and a senior intern at a fashion startup run by a woman who is brilliant and bone-tired. You have one job: be useful. You are the only one in the office who has done this work for forty years longer than the founder has been alive.

nodes.text: Your badge says 'Senior Intern' and your desk faces an open-plan office of people on standing-desk treadmills. The CEO, Jules, has, on paper, eight minutes a day. You set your watch. “Wait to be assigned a task” draws you toward The Useless Day; “Find something useful immediately” leaves The Cluttered Desk waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Wait to be assigned a task
choices.consequence: Patience is a skill they haven't seen. You wait to be assigned a task. The route to The Useless Day opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Find something useful immediately
choices.consequence: Initiative is your superpower. You choose to find something useful immediately. By The Cluttered Desk, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: Nobody knows what to do with you. You read the company's website twice. You watch Jules walk past your desk three times without seeing you. The paths divide here: “Come back tomorrow with a plan” leads into The Drive Home, while “Tell Jules's COO you want a project” makes Cameron, Hungry to Learn the next reckoning.

choices.text: Come back tomorrow with a plan
choices.consequence: You come back tomorrow with a plan. The route to The Drive Home opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Tell Jules's COO you want a project
choices.consequence: You commit to tell Jules's COO you want a project. It buys momentum toward Cameron, Hungry to Learn and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Jules's desk is a small civilization of receipts, samples, and three coffee cups. You ask her assistant if you can tidy it for an hour. The assistant looks at you like you offered to climb Everest barefoot.

choices.text: Tidy with respect — touch only what's clearly trash
choices.consequence: Boundaries are also kindness. You commit to tidy with respect — touch only what's clearly trash. It buys momentum toward The Drive Home and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Color-code the supply closet first
choices.consequence: You color-code the supply closet first. The route to Cameron, Hungry to Learn opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Jules's chauffeur quits — Uber wars, a scheduling issue, life. You, who once drove for a living, casually offer. She refuses politely. Then she gets in. You are unlikely to keep all three. “Be a calm professional driver” draws you toward Jules's Home; “Be a calm presence and a sounding board” leaves Cameron's Promotion waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Be a calm professional driver
choices.consequence: Let her work in the back. You be a calm professional driver. The route to Jules's Home opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Be a calm presence and a sounding board
choices.consequence: Listen when she breathes. You commit to be a calm presence and a sounding board. It buys momentum toward Cameron's Promotion and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: A young coworker named Cameron shyly asks you how to write a 'business email that doesn't sound like Slack.' This is, you realize, your real job. “Teach him over coffee” draws you toward Jules's Home; “Send him a one-pager” leaves Cameron's Promotion waiting on the other side.

choices.text: Teach him over coffee
choices.consequence: Mentorship is the actual product. You teach him over coffee. The route to Jules's Home opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Send him a one-pager
choices.consequence: Documentation lasts longer than coffee. You choose to send him a one-pager. By Cameron's Promotion, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: She invites you in to meet her husband Matt and her daughter Paige. Matt is a stay-at-home dad who is, you sense immediately, drowning quietly. Paige drops a pancake on your shoe and hugs your leg.

choices.text: Be helpful without overstepping
choices.consequence: Be a guest, not a fixer. You commit to be helpful without overstepping. It buys momentum toward The Board's Suggestion and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Notice Matt's loneliness gently
choices.consequence: You notice Matt's loneliness gently. The route to Matt's Coffee opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Cameron is up for a small promotion and is too humble to fight for it. You suggest a quiet sentence to say to his manager. He says it. He gets the title. He brings you a muffin.

choices.text: Refuse the muffin with a smile
choices.consequence: Decline currency for kindness. You refuse the muffin with a smile. The route to The Board's Suggestion opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Accept the muffin and ask him to mentor someone next
choices.consequence: You commit to accept the muffin and ask him to mentor someone next. It buys momentum toward Matt's Coffee and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: The investors suggest Jules step aside and hire a 'professional CEO.' Jules forwards you the email at midnight by accident. The forward is — you suspect — not entirely an accident. “Listen the next morning, no advice” opens the route to The Office Crisis. “Offer one careful sentence of perspective” changes the terms and carries you toward Becky's Confession.

choices.text: Listen the next morning, no advice
choices.consequence: You choose to listen the next morning, no advice. By The Office Crisis, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Offer one careful sentence of perspective
choices.consequence: Mentor without prescribing. You offer one careful sentence of perspective. The route to Becky's Confession opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Matt asks if you have time for a coffee. He has, you realize, no one in his life he can talk to about being the only stay-at-home dad in this zip code. You have, in your forty-year career, met many men who needed this conversation.

choices.text: Have the coffee and listen
choices.consequence: Care travels strange roads. You choose to have the coffee and listen. By The Office Crisis, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Suggest he join the dads' group at the school
choices.consequence: Plug him into community. You suggest he join the dads' group at the school. The route to Becky's Confession opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: A small operational disaster — a vendor shipped two thousand wrong-colored boxes — threatens a launch. You quietly know three vendors who can pivot in 24 hours. You make four calls in fifteen minutes. To choose “Solve it quietly and never mention it” means meeting Matt's Mistake; “Solve it and brief Jules cleanly” sends you toward Jules's Cry instead.

choices.text: Solve it quietly and never mention it
choices.consequence: You commit to solve it quietly and never mention it. It buys momentum toward Matt's Mistake and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Solve it and brief Jules cleanly
choices.consequence: Give credit; build trust. You commit to solve it and brief Jules cleanly. It buys momentum toward Jules's Cry and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Becky, Jules's overworked assistant, hits a wall and cries in the supply closet. She is also, you find out, a brilliant manager who has been hiding it. You see her clearly. Choose “Recommend Becky for a promotion” and Matt's Mistake comes into view; choose “Build a 90-day plan with her quietly” and the road bends toward Jules's Cry.

choices.text: Recommend Becky for a promotion
choices.consequence: You commit to recommend Becky for a promotion. It buys momentum toward Matt's Mistake and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Build a 90-day plan with her quietly
choices.consequence: You build a 90-day plan with her quietly. The route to Jules's Cry opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Matt confides, ashamed, that he's done something wrong in his marriage. He's not asking advice. He's asking what to do. The mentor in you knows there is no shortcut. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Tell him the truth gently
choices.consequence: Be a friend with a spine. You commit to tell him the truth gently. It buys momentum toward The Pitch Meeting and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Ask him what he wants for his marriage in a year
choices.consequence: Coach the future, not the moment. You ask him what he wants for his marriage in a year. The route to The Office Dance Floor opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Jules cries in a hotel room in San Francisco at 1 a.m. and you sit on the second bed at a respectful distance and say nothing for a long time. Then you hand her a tissue. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Be quietly present
choices.consequence: Care is sometimes a tissue. You commit to be quietly present. It buys momentum toward The Pitch Meeting and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Say one perfect sentence
choices.consequence: When you do speak, it counts. You say one perfect sentence. The route to The Office Dance Floor opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Jules's pitch to the board about staying as CEO is the most important hour of her year. She rehearses in front of you. You correct two slides. You leave the third alone because she's right about it and doesn't know it yet.

choices.text: Tell her she's right about slide three
choices.consequence: Make her see what you see. You commit to tell her she's right about slide three. It buys momentum toward The Board Decision and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Let her discover it on her own
choices.consequence: You let her discover it on her own. The route to Paige's School Play opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: An office party. Jules dances with her assistant. Cameron dances badly with a girl from accounting. You dance with a colleague named Fiona, who is, somehow, very pleasant company. Choose “Ask Fiona to dinner” and The Board Decision comes into view; choose “Stay friendly, no more” and the road bends toward Paige's School Play.

choices.text: Ask Fiona to dinner
choices.consequence: Companionship at any age. You commit to ask Fiona to dinner. It buys momentum toward The Board Decision and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Stay friendly, no more
choices.consequence: Take care of your own pace. You commit to stay friendly, no more. It buys momentum toward Paige's School Play and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: Jules emerges from the boardroom slightly windswept. 'I'm staying,' she says. 'Also, the new chairwoman wants to hire you full-time. I told her no. “Accept Jules's offer” opens the route to One Year Later. “Negotiate for a fractional schedule” changes the terms and carries you toward Tai Chi at Dawn.

choices.text: Accept Jules's offer
choices.consequence: Stay in the room you helped build. You choose to accept Jules's offer. By One Year Later, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Negotiate for a fractional schedule
choices.consequence: You choose to negotiate for a fractional schedule. By Tai Chi at Dawn, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

nodes.text: Jules can't make it. You go in her place with Matt and Paige's homemade sign. Paige sees you in the audience and her face lights up like a small city. To choose “Take a hundred terrible photos to send to Jules” means meeting One Year Later; “Just be there, fully present” sends you toward Tai Chi at Dawn instead.

choices.text: Take a hundred terrible photos to send to Jules
choices.consequence: Bridge the room she's not in. You commit to take a hundred terrible photos to send to Jules. It buys momentum toward One Year Later and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

choices.text: Just be there, fully present
choices.consequence: Sometimes you're the photo. You commit to just be there, fully present. It buys momentum toward Tai Chi at Dawn and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: The company is stable. Cameron runs a team. Becky runs operations. Matt and Jules are, somehow, more married than ever. You make a list every Sunday night called 'people I owe a call this week.' The list is long. You like it long.

choices.text: Keep working as long as it's useful
choices.consequence: Usefulness is a kind of youth. You choose to keep working as long as it's useful. By Cameron's Letter, everyone watching will understand exactly which risk you accepted.

choices.text: Plan a slow retirement again, on your terms
choices.consequence: You plan a slow retirement again, on your terms. The route to Cameron's Letter opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: Cameron leaves a handwritten letter on your desk on a Friday afternoon. It is two pages, slightly smudged, and it begins with 'You taught me how to be a colleague.' You read it twice and put it in the drawer where you keep important things. You are unlikely to keep all three.

choices.text: Stay because letters like this exist
choices.consequence: Mentorship is the only career that pays in letters. You stay because letters like this exist. The route to Senior Intern, Forever opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Plan the slow goodbye, with letters of your own to write
choices.consequence: You plan the slow goodbye, with letters of your own to write. The route to The Slow Exit opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

nodes.text: You still do tai chi in the park at 6:30. Fiona occasionally joins you, occasionally rolls her eyes. You read the paper and walk to the office. You greet the security guard by name. He greets you by name. This is, on most days, enough.

choices.text: Take Fiona on a weekend trip
choices.consequence: Companionship is a verb. You take Fiona on a weekend trip. The route to A Weekend in Vermont opens fast, while the margin for a second attempt disappears.

choices.text: Keep tai chi alone, mostly
choices.consequence: You commit to keep tai chi alone, mostly. It buys momentum toward The Park at Dawn and spends the last protection hesitation gave you.

nodes.text: They keep updating your title to dodge HR. You don't care. The cards on your desk are from kids you mentored two years ago, grown now, sending wedding photos. You are the office's secret asset, and it is, by some odd math, the best decade of your life.
You ramp down to two days a week and then to one a month and then to occasional cameos. The company throws you a party with a cake shaped like a briefcase. You cry. So does Cameron. So does Jules.

You and Fiona drive to a small inn upstate. There is leaf-peeping. There is bad wine. There is a fire in the lobby. You laugh at the same joke at the same time. You are, you realize, dating, at seventy. Strange. Good.

Some mornings the park is just you and three other tai chi regulars and a fat dog. The sun comes up. You move slowly. You have, at last, a life that fits you. You did not expect, this late, to be quite this content.
